summary: The Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) is China's main full scholarship for international students. For 2026/27 it covered tuition, a university dormitory or housing subsidy, comprehensive medical insurance and a monthly stipend (CNY 3,000 for master's, CNY 3,500 for PhD). Winners have a clear study plan, strong grades, a pre-admission letter from a Chinese university (often with a supervisor's support), and a complete, correctly certified document pack.
lookfor: Academic excellence shown in notarized transcripts and degree certificates
A focused study or research plan that fits the target university and supervisor
A pre-admission letter from the target Chinese university (required in 2026/27 embassy calls)
Two strong recommendation letters from professors or associate professors
Language readiness: IELTS/TOEFL for English-taught programmes or HSK 4 for Chinese-taught ones
Complete, correct documents: medical form, non-criminal record and valid passport
cycle: The 2026/27 round ran roughly November 2025 to February 2026 (embassy deadlines 15–20 February in several countries), with document review in late Feb–March, university/CSC review March–July and admission notices in late June–July. Expect the 2027/28 round to open around November–December 2026: watch the Chinese Embassy in Nigeria and your target universities now.

eligibility.q: Are you a non-Chinese citizen in good physical and mental health with a valid passport?
eligibility.no: CSC is only for foreign nationals. Fix passport issues first (the passport should be valid at least 12 months beyond your start date).

eligibility.q: For a master's: do you hold a bachelor's degree and are you under 35? For a PhD: do you hold a master's degree and are you under 40?
eligibility.no: Over the age limit? Consider Commonwealth or university awards without age caps. Without the required degree, apply one level lower or wait until you graduate.

eligibility.q: Do you have no record of disciplinary, security or criminal offences (and can you get a police certificate)?
eligibility.no: A non-criminal record certificate is required; you cannot win without one.

eligibility.q: Can you meet the language rule: IELTS/TOEFL (or an English-medium degree, if the university accepts it) for English-taught programmes, or HSK 4 for Chinese-taught master's/PhD?
eligibility.no: Book IELTS now, or pick an English-taught programme. Many universities accept proof of English-medium instruction – confirm with each one.

eligibility.q: Are you not currently studying in China on another Chinese government scholarship?
eligibility.no: Check the rules in the current call; you cannot hold two Chinese government scholarships at once.

steps.title: Choose your route: embassy (Type A) or university (Type B)
steps.why: CSC has two main doors with separate deadlines. Many applicants use both in the same year to raise their chances.
do: Type A (bilateral/embassy): you apply on campuschina.org using the agency number in the Chinese Embassy in Nigeria's notice; the embassy nominates you.
Type B (Chinese University Program): you apply directly to a Chinese university that holds CSC places; the university nominates you.
Write down which universities you will target and which route each uses.
Check the official portal and your embassy's notice for current rules.
tips: Use the same strong study plan for both routes, adjusted to each university.
avoid: Paying an agent for 'guaranteed' CSC places – the official application is free on campuschina.org.
check: I know which route(s) I will use and why.

steps.title: Understand what decides the award
steps.why: Universities and CSC pick students whose plans fit their programmes and whose papers are complete.
do: List the 'lookfor' points in this guide.
Note where you are weak (e.g. no publication, low English score) and how to fix it before the deadline.
Compare CSC with MEXT and GKS if you are also eligible.
tips: A supervisor who wants you is often the strongest factor at university level.
avoid: Applying to famous universities only; competition there is fierce.
check: I know my strongest selling points.

steps.title: Shortlist universities and contact supervisors
steps.why: A pre-admission letter from your target university was required in 2026/27 embassy calls; for PhD, a supervisor's support is usually essential.
do: Search university international-student sites for CSC-eligible programmes in your field (English-taught if you lack HSK).
Pick 3 universities: one top, one strong, one regional with your field.
Find 1–2 professors per university whose papers match your topic.
Email each a short message: who you are, a 3-line research idea, why their lab, with CV attached.
Follow up after 2 weeks; ask how to get a pre-admission (acceptance) letter.
tips: Mention one of the professor's recent papers to show you read it.
avoid: Mass emailing the same generic message to 100 professors.
check: I have at least one professor or university willing to support me.

steps.title: Build your timeline and create your Campus China account
steps.why: University deadlines (often Dec–Mar) and the embassy deadline (Feb in 2026) are different; documents like the police certificate expire after 6 months.
do: Create an account at campuschina.org.
List each university's own deadline and the embassy deadline.
Plan: police certificate and medical in the 3 months before the deadline (both must be recent).
Set reminders to check the Chinese Embassy in Nigeria website weekly from November.
tips: Keep a spreadsheet: university, route, agency number, deadline, status.
avoid: Getting the medical too early – it is valid for 6 months only.
check: I have an account and all deadlines written down.

steps.title: Get notarized degree certificates and transcripts
steps.why: CSC asks for notarized copies of your highest degree and transcripts in English or Chinese.
do: Request transcripts from your university's Exams & Records office.
Take your certificate and transcripts to a Notary Public (in Nigeria, many notaries are at the High Court registry or private law firms) for notarization.
Scan the notarized copies in colour at high resolution (around 300 dpi) as PDF/JPG.
If you have not graduated, get a letter proving you are a final-year student.
tips: Ask the notary to stamp every page.
avoid: Blurry scans – unreadable documents get rejected.
check: My notarized copies are clear and complete.

steps.title: Do the Foreigner Physical Examination Form
steps.why: Required for study over 6 months; it must be signed by a physician, stamped by the hospital, with a stamped photo, and is valid for 6 months.
do: Download the Foreigner Physical Examination Form from campuschina.org or your university.
Go to a government or teaching hospital; do all tests listed (blood tests, chest X-ray, ECG).
Make sure the doctor signs, the hospital stamps, and your photo is stamped across.
Scan the form and all lab reports.
tips: Federal Medical Centres and university teaching hospitals are familiar with this form.
avoid: Missing a single test – incomplete forms are rejected.
check: Form signed, stamped, photo sealed, all lab reports attached.

steps.title: Get a non-criminal record certificate and language proof
steps.why: The police certificate must be issued within 6 months of submission; a language score is needed for most programmes.
do: Nigerians: apply for a Police Character Certificate from the Nigeria Police Force (allow several weeks).
Book IELTS (or TOEFL) if your university requires it; HSK 4 for Chinese-taught master's/PhD.
If your degree was taught in English, request an English-medium letter from your university (accepted by some universities).
Check your passport is valid; scan the data page.
tips: Start the police certificate early; it is often the slowest document.
avoid: Using a certificate older than 6 months.
check: I have a valid police certificate, passport scan and language proof.

steps.title: Write the study plan / research proposal
steps.why: It shows the university and CSC what you will study and why; for PhD it is often read by your future supervisor.
steps.prompt: Your study or research plan in China.
steps.limit: 2026/27 embassy calls: more than 800 words for postgraduates. Some universities ask for more (e.g. about 3,000 words master's / 6,000 words PhD at Sun Yat-sen) – follow each university.
do: Title and short introduction: who you are and your field.
Background and problem: why it matters in Nigeria/Africa and globally.
Objectives and research questions.
Methods and why this Chinese university/lab is the right place.
Timeline across the degree years.
Expected outcomes and your plans after graduation.
tips: Link to China–Africa cooperation only if it is genuine to your topic.
avoid: Going under the minimum word count.
Using a generic plan that names the wrong university.
check: It meets the word count and names the right university and supervisor.

steps.title: Get two recommendation letters from professors
steps.why: Two letters from professors or associate professors are required for graduate programmes.
do: Ask two senior lecturers who taught or supervised you (Professor/Associate Professor rank where possible).
Send them your CV, study plan, and a note on what to highlight.
Ask for signed letters on university letterhead, in English, with contact details.
Scan the signed letters as PDF.
tips: If your prospective Chinese supervisor writes support, keep it separate as the pre-admission evidence.
avoid: Letters from junior staff only, if senior ones are available.
check: I have two signed letters from senior academics.

steps.title: Fill the CSC online application
steps.why: The system requires exact program category and agency number; a wrong number sends your file to the wrong place.
do: Log in to campuschina.org and start a new application.
Choose the program category (Type A for embassy, or Type B for university) and enter the agency number from the official notice or university.
Enter personal data exactly as in your passport.
Choose your universities and programmes (match your pre-admission letter).
Upload all documents; check each file opens.
Submit and download the application form PDF.
tips: Print the PDF form; many universities and embassies need a signed copy.
avoid: Using an agency number copied from a blog without checking the official notice.
check: The system shows 'submitted' and I have the PDF.

steps.title: Send copies to universities and the embassy as instructed
steps.why: Many universities also need their own online application or a paper copy, and embassies may need hard copies.
do: Complete each university's own online application if they have one.
Submit hard copies to the Chinese Embassy if the notice asks.
Keep tracking numbers and confirmation emails.
tips: Email the international office to confirm they received your file.
avoid: Assuming CSC submission alone is enough for Type B.
check: Every university and the embassy confirmed receipt.

steps.title: Prepare for interviews and review
steps.why: Embassies may interview during document review, and universities often interview online.
do: Watch your email and phone; reply within 24 hours.
Prepare to explain your study plan in 3 minutes and answer: Why China? Why this university? What after?
Test your internet, camera and microphone for online interviews.
tips: Know your proposed supervisor's recent work.
avoid: Missing an interview email in spam.
check: I can explain my plan clearly and briefly.

steps.title: Results, JW201/202 form and X1 visa
steps.why: Admission notices come around late June–July; you need the admission notice and JW form to apply for a student visa.
do: Check campuschina.org and your email for results.
Receive your Admission Notice and JW201/JW202 form from the university.
Apply for an X1 student visa at the Chinese visa centre with these documents.
Budget for your own flight (airfare was not listed in the 2026/27 coverage) and first-month costs.
tips: Ask the university for arrival instructions and airport pickup.
check: I have admission notice, JW form and visa.

faq.q: Do I need a supervisor before applying?
faq.a: You need a pre-admission letter from the university for 2026/27 embassy applications; for PhD this usually means a supervisor agreed to take you.
The 2026/27 embassy call lists tuition, accommodation, stipend and insurance, but not airfare. Budget for your own ticket unless your offer says otherwise.

faq.q: Can I apply to both the embassy and universities?
faq.a: Yes, many applicants use both routes in the same year. Check each notice's rules.

faq.q: Do I need to speak Chinese?
faq.a: Not for English-taught programmes. Chinese-taught master's/PhD programmes need HSK 4.
Under 35 for master's and under 40 for PhD in the 2026/27 calls.
The CSC application on campuschina.org is free; some universities charge their own application fee.
